title: Dynamic stage-aware communication scheduler with kernel probing
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Multi-GPU models with mixed tensor and pipeline parallelism suffer from suboptimal overlap between NCCL communication and kernel execution, and from conservative kernel selection at stage boundaries. This results in higher tail latency during prefill and decode phases and reduced overall throughput.

Goal: Build a scheduler that: (1) observes runtime kernel performance and communication patterns (kernel probing), (2) defers or advances cross-stage kernel swaps to maximize overlap with NCCL collective ops, and (3) adapts prefill/decode scheduling per-request to trade latency vs throughput.

Success metrics: reduce P95 token latency by >= 15% for multi-GPU configs with pipeline depth >=2; increase average NCCL overlap fraction by >= 25%; avoid >2% regression in single-GPU or small-batch throughput; maintain deterministic outputs for seeded requests.

Approach summary:
- Lightweight kernel probing: instrument a short microbenchmark run at stage startup (few warmup tokens) to measure kernel vs memcpy cost under current sequence length and device temperature.
- Stage-aware policy: use probing signals to decide whether to run larger prefill batches at the stage or to split prefill across stages to expose more NCCL time.
- Boundary deferral window: allow small, bounded postponement (configurable ms) of stage transitions when a large NCCL op is imminent, so that GPU kernels from the next stage can start while NCCL is in flight.
- Conditional NCCL priming: insert a tiny NCCL AllReduce of an empty tensor to wake up NIC/queues in high-latency setups when helpful.
- Kernel selection hints: expose real-time hint channel from scheduler to kernel selector to pick algorithms with lower latency tail when overlap is expected.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Complexity vs determinism: deferral changes ordering; we will provide a deterministic mode that disables deferrals for reproducible inference.
- Safety margins: ensure deferral windows never increase user-visible time when NCCL is not the bottleneck (policy falls back to no-deferral).
- Overhead budget: probing must add <1% token cost on average; conditional priming should be gated by heuristics (cold NICs, known high-latency links).
implementation_notes: We will implement scheduler as a new runtime component (stage-scheduler) with a CompactTelemetry protobuf wire format. The stage-scheduler exposes a per-request decision API (sync) and a broadcast hint channel to the kernel selector. Probing will reuse existing timing hooks already present in the runtime to avoid extra CUDA events where possible. Defaults: 4 warmup tokens for probing, deferral window max 6ms, priming enabled only for inter-rack configs by default.
testing_plan: Unit tests for decision logic; integration tests on multi-GPU CI harness (4xA100 and 8xH100 matrices); microbenchmarks for kernel probe overhead; end-to-end perf runs with synthetic Llama and MPT workloads (seq_len 512/2048, batch 1/8). Add chaos tests that introduce transient NCCL slowdowns to validate fallbacks. Compare against baseline ENG-16489 orchestration runs.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated off by default in runtime-1.32 branch. 2) Canary on internal Dedicated cluster for low-traffic models. 3) Gradual ramp to 10% of traffic with perf regression guardrails. 4) Enable by default after 2 weeks of telemetry showing no regressions. Include opt-out flag per-deployment and deterministic override.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: misclassifying kernel vs comm bound leading to worse tail latency. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and automatic disable when P95 increases. Risk: added complexity in kernel selection path. Mitigation: keep hint channel simple (3 enums) and fall back to existing selector.
